caseReviews.rationale: Resolve the archived replacement-identity gap using the named Week 2 primary right guard. Keep the archived healthy-player baseline for this individual estimate; do not adjudicate a future permanent lineup or change a carried rating.
caseReviews.roleRationale: The coach names Barber at right guard for Week 2, replacing the role previously occupied by the unavailable Teven Jenkins. Preserve registry position RT; the football source establishes the actual same-group RG assignment.
caseReviews.baselineRationale: Model only added starting-right-guard duties. Reporting puts Barber on the second team before the vacancy; the adjacent starting center and right tackle remain in their positions. No simultaneous occupied starting-line role is treated as free replacement value. Any wider group conflict is reserved for paired adoption.
caseReviews.assumptionRationale: Treat the documented Week 2 primary right guard as the effective replacement under the approved PRIMARY_REPLACEMENT convention. This is not a claim of every snap, empirical calibration, or complete team injury loss.

caseReviews.rationale: Add the previously omitted Parrish absence as an individual reported-primary estimate, with final inactive reporting and actual replacement participation. This is not a final Tampa Bay team total.
caseReviews.roleRationale: Game-day reporting identifies Morrison as the expected replacement starter; official prior role reporting identifies the same vacant position and the postgame report corroborates his participation. The assignment is labelled REPORTED_PRIMARY, not a complete snap allocation.
caseReviews.baselineRationale: Preserve Morrison's existing reserve/subpackage duties and value only the added duties in Parrish's position. The club describes Morrison replacing the injured player in the lineup rather than moving an identified other starter. This is a documented modelling assessment; a conflicting simultaneous role at team-level adoption must block reuse.
caseReviews.assumptionRationale: Use Morrison as the reported primary replacement rather than inventing a committee allocation. This is the approved individual modelling convention, not a statistical interval or a declaration that every team absence is reconciled.
